claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex - he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! Thank you for reaching out. I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask a few questions about your circumstances.

Firstly, are you responsible for Alex? By this I mean, does Alex live with you, or do you contribute towards the cost of looking after him at an amount of at least the same as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest child)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me - he lives with his mum. But I do help out financially. I contribute about £30 a week towards his upkeep - you know, helping with clothes, school things, that sort of stuff.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. It's helpful to know you contribute £30 a week towards Alex's upkeep.

Since Alex lives with his mum rather than with you, I need to ask: is Alex's mum already claiming Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know.

I have another question: Is Alex's mum eligible to claim Child Benefit herself? For example, does she live in the UK and is she responsible for Alex's day-to-day care since he lives with her?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she does live in the UK and she looks after Alex day-to-day since he lives with her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Let me now ask about your own circumstances. Are you currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not living in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since you're living abroad, could you tell me a bit more about your situation? Specifically:

Are you a UK national working abroad for the UK government (for example, as a civil servant or member of the armed forces), or are you employed by a company that is registered or has its head office in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of those apply to me. I'm just living and working abroad in a regular job.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me review the eligibility rules to make sure I give you accurate information about your situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience while I reviewed the eligibility rules.

Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

1. **UK Residency Requirement**: To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. Since you are living and working abroad in a regular job (and are not a Crown servant or working for a UK-registered company), you don't meet this fundamental requirement.

2. **Alex's Mother Has Priority**: Although you do contribute £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which exceeds the Child Benefit amount), Alex lives with his mother in the UK, and she is responsible for his day-to-day care. This means she would be the person with priority to claim Child Benefit for him.

**My suggestion**: Since Alex's mother lives in the UK with Alex and is responsible for his care, she would be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him. It may be worth encouraging her to make a claim, as she appears to meet the eligibility criteria.

I hope this helps clarify your situation. Please let me know if you have any other questions.
